Gina

subject: An update on early voting numbers in key battleground states:
body:
We’re only sending this to our most engaged supporters [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/87341?t=1&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr)
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 13 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=2&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr). If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=3&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=4&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=5&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr). Derek, **Early voting is officially underway in many states across the country.** As one of our top grassroots supporters, we want to keep you in the loop on the DNC’s strategy for the final 13 days before Election Day. Please take a minute to read this memo — we made this specifically for our most engaged supporters. _**2026 Early Voting Update for Derek Willis_**
* As of this morning, voters are casting their ballots in 37 states. **That means time is running out to turn out voters in key battlegrounds and help them make a plan to vote.**
* Currently, early voting in **Georgia is pacing _ahead_** of early voting numbers during the 2022 midterm elections, and polling favors Democrats maintaining their hold on this critical Senate seat.
* In **North Carolina, Democrats need to _flip_ the open Senate seat** to help take the majority this year and are currently **pacing ahead of their early ballots returned at this point in 2022.** Democrats have consistently led Republicans in polling this year, but turnout will be key.
* **Democrats are also working to flip a Senate seat in Iowa this year.** Currently, early ballots returned are **outpacing this point in 2022,** and polling predicts an incredibly tight race. Traditionally, most Iowans return their ballots on Election Day, so there’s still a chance to reach as many voters as possible across the state, help them make their voices heard, and flip this seat.
* **Michigan is currently pacing close to its early vote numbers from 2022, but there’s still time to change that if we act now.** This is a _must-win state_ for Democrats if we want to flip the Senate this year, and **polling currently shows that the race is neck and neck.**
* **Maine's Senate seat** is another must-flip seat for Democrats this year. Currently **leading ahead of early vote numbers from 2022,** this will also be an incredibly tight race.
* In **Ohio,** Democrats are also working to flip the Senate seat to win a majority, and the race is rated as another toss-up. Most Ohioans vote on Election Day, so it’s critical that we ensure every Ohio Democrat is ready to cast their ballot come November 3.

With just 13 days until Election Day, the DNC is strategically moving resources to the states and districts across the country that need the most support in these final weeks. We’re deploying organizers and volunteers to key districts to knock doors, we’re sending poll observers to polling locations to ensure the election is free, fair, and the results are trustworthy, and we’re making calls every day into states across the country to reach voters we might not otherwise. Derek, we hope you found this memo helpful. Keeping our top grassroots supporters fully informed and up-to-date on our strategic priorities is a top priority for our team. [**We hope you’ll consider chipping in today to fund our on-the-ground organizing efforts in the final days before Election Day and help lay the groundwork to win this year and beyond. The DNC is best positioned to distribute resources where and when they’re needed most, and every dollar we receive goes directly to the front lines to elect Democrats up and down the ballot nationwide.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&refcode=em_20261021_9996_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.GS9qR7&amount=7&refcode=em_20261021_9996_fr&t=7&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr)**

[1] He claims to support term limits, but has already broken his pledge to serve no more than 12 years in the House. [2] He insists he's committed to protecting children, yet he's done nothing to demand accountability or unseal the most infamous case of child endangerment, the Epstein files. ---
Hi friend, it's Deb.

With Election Day right around the corner, I’ve been on the road, listening to as many New Mexicans as I can. My focus is making sure people have the opportunity to ask questions, share what’s on their minds, and hear directly from me about my vision for New Mexico’s future before they head to the polls.
The energy on the ground is incredible! Folks all over our state are ready to build a future where everyone can thrive. **[_If you’re ready to make this a reality, will you chip in $5 right now so I can reach the final undecided voters in these last 13 days and win?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17378?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)**
| | [Pitch in $5 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17378?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
---
Here’s a look at some of the stops I’ve made in _just_ the past week:
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=4&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
I spoke to voters in the South Valley about how high the stakes are at this moment — from the affordability crisis and Trump’s reckless attacks on our state to our fight to protect our sacred land for future generations.

Each conversation reminds me what makes New Mexico so special — and why it’s so important to keep fighting for a better future.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=5&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
I joined a meeting of the organization Drinking Liberally in Albuquerque to answer questions about my plan to improve schools, increase access to healthcare, and build safer communities for our families. I made it clear that I’m ready to deliver real results and get things done for New Mexicans.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=6&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
I was joined by Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer in Rio Rancho, where we discussed the importance of Democratic governors who serve as firewalls against federal abuses of power. With Trump escalating his attacks on New Mexico, we need proven leaders who will protect our fundamental rights, our land, and our people.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=7&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
I was joined by Sen. Elizabeth Warren to discuss the crucial need to protect and expand universal childcare in New Mexico and how my plan to lower costs, build more homes, and cut the red tape to make home buying easier for first-time homeowners will support New Mexicans.

Every conversation has been a powerful reminder of why I’m running: to listen, bring people together, and deliver real results for families in every corner of our state. All across our beautiful state, New Mexicans want the same things: affordable, accessible healthcare, a strong education for their kids, safe communities, and the ability to pay the rent and buy groceries in the same month.
That’s what I’m fighting for. **_But right now, we’re running out of time to make sure we keep New Mexico blue._**
**With only 13 days until Election Day, every door, every conversation, and every vote matters more than ever before.[_Please, will you chip in $5 or more right now to help power my campaign for Governor and reach voters in every corner of New Mexico?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=8&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)**
| | [Pitch in $5 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17378?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=9&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
---
Together, we’re going to build a New Mexico for all New Mexicans.

Thank you, and be fierce,
Deb

Peter, Have you heard? Do you feel it? [Early](https://clicksp.votejustinearly.com/f/a/zEGAvwyfzIHN8bQh1v3SgA~~/AAPPABA~/mc23ckxzL-W5sU-v7HBT3DrvOJpWBv_Zhg3ajiogun2zOsU8Qg5WlNMc90Ezp9YxYm6-MjVnTtMN5TLf1OeKBo3kuN1pIVJkuNQAOv88AYARi-QE8KeOZ0DcnG3J2Qs2vfztCJJSkO_iUFL8FQN8WBR9eoB_d7CDD9NdK3rlh3BOhKW5s8kXXMz3AYf23p4Qw-U07uqAwxdEunxchCe_yHF8xiL8PSBqRFrmvDIKew5re5jP5NJdEGuTd68jjvZvZ9KCIQIPCoZU07iFKxXTsg~~) voting is underway, and our district is show up in a **big** way! In Bell County, near center of TX-31, 8,796 people voted on day one, a midterm record. In-person turnout was more than 50% above opening day in 2022, and over 14,000 people voted in person in the first two days. In Williamson County, about 13,500 had voted by 2 p.m. on opening day, nearly matching the roughly 15,000 who voted on the entire first day in 2022. This surge builds on a record-setting primary, when Democratic early turnout jumped 123% over 2022. Texas also has about 1.4 million more registered voters than it did four years ago. And earlier this year, Democrat Taylor Rehmet won the Senate District 9 runoff by 14 points in a district Trump carried by 17. We have a movement! Turnout alone does not tell us who people voted for, but analysts say Democrats are more enthusiastic this cycle. When a district that has been taken for granted wakes up, seats flip. Let's flip this seat! Here is how you can help:

| | Peter,

I just walked off the debate stage where one thing was clear: We need leaders who are going to put Minnesota first.

If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=2&akid=10019%2E22930333%2E6H1oTv). subject: You’re one of a select few
body:
Hey, Peter – I wanted to reach out directly.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1728&source=&t=1&akid=4821%2E124072%2EZ9Ya5k) | | | |

Peter, not everyone will be getting this email.
I’m only reaching out to a select group of folks – people who haven’t donated to our campaign yet, but have stayed engaged with our updates and might be inclined to chip in for the first time today. **Your name was on that list.**
First, I want to say thank you for even opening this message. Your inbox is likely packed with emails like this right now, so I don’t take your time and attention for granted.
Here’s the deal: **The deadline to hit our fundraising goal to fund our FINAL TV ads before Election Day is at 11:59 p.m. tonight. To ensure we have the resources to reach every last voter between now and Nov. 3, I set an ambitious $500,000 goal for our team to reach before then.**
Frankly, we’re running out of time to make our case to North Carolinians – and a recent poll of likely voters shows that 7% are still undecided.
If they all end up siding with my MAGA opponent because we let far-right super PACs have the final word on the airwaves, **our lead in this race could shrink overnight.** With Senate control at stake here, that’s a risk we simply cannot afford to take.
Unlike my opponent, Michael Whatley, this campaign is not bankrolled by billionaires. More than 95% of our donations last quarter were $100 or less, so when I say this movement is powered by small-dollar support from people like you, I mean it, Peter.
**That’s why I’m personally asking for your help today.[_Will you please chip in your first $5 donation to help us reach this ambitious goal by the midnight deadline? The results of this battleground race will shape the future of our country, so your support couldn’t come at a more urgent time._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1728&amount=5&t=8&akid=4821%2E124072%2EZ9Ya5k)**

Roy Cooper

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

name: Kylie Glatfelter
subject: Beau Bayh Can't Have It Both Ways on Girls' Sports
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE
body:
No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-e-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-x/) **For Immediate Release:** October 21, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, [kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)**Beau Bayh Is Proud to Have JD Ford on His Team. What Does That Say About His Judgment?****Indianapolis, Ind. **- Of all the endorsements Beau Bayh could have celebrated, he chose one from a senator who voted against protecting girls' sports, against extending those protections to women's college athletics, and against banning gender-transition procedures for minors.In June, Bayh posted on [social media](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-r/): "Honored to have earned the endorsement of my friend, State Senator JD Ford. I'm proud to have you on our team!" When the [Indiana Capital Chronicle](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-y/) asked Bayh if he supports Indiana's ban on boys in girls' sports, he waved the whole thing away as a "nonissue." Ford voted against the [2022 law](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-j/) protecting girls' sports, which took effect after Republicans overrode a veto. His reasoning? He said it "does not solve an issue." In 2025, Ford was one of just six senators to vote against extending those protections to women's college athletics. The bill passed 42-6. In 2023, Ford also voted against legislation [banning gender-transition procedures for minors](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-t/). The bill passed the Senate 36-12 and ultimately became law. Hoosier parents will remember those votes. Beau Bayh looked at that record and called it worth being proud of. So what does that say about his judgment? Either he agrees with Ford's votes, or he's willing to overlook them. Neither is the judgment Hoosiers want in a Secretary of State. He can't tell Hoosier parents he's on their side after welcoming the man who voted against them onto his team. He can't have it both ways."Fairness for our daughters isn't negotiable, and it isn't a nonissue," said Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling. "Who you're proud to stand beside tells Hoosiers everything about your judgment, and Beau Bayh is proud to stand beside someone who voted against that fairness. Hoosiers deserve a Secretary of State who shares their values and says the same thing no matter who's in the room. Max Engling is that candidate."Max Engling, the Republican nominee for Secretary of State, has said plainly that men should not play in women's sports. It is not a position he has to be asked about twice. Beau Bayh, by contrast, called the question a nonissue and then celebrated the man who voted against women. Hoosiers are still waiting on a straight answer.### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-d/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-h/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-k/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-u/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-p/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. We have less than two weeks left to beat John Sununu and help take back the United States Senate.
Last Saturday in Exeter, we gathered with Governor Gavin Newsom, Senator Maggie Hassan, Cinde Warmington, Stefany Shaheen, and a room full of Granite Staters who are ready to finish this race strong.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd95e8d9-ce8e-4566-9d12-3652a050475f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The people who will power us over the finish line are the ones who filled that room along with those knocking doors, making calls, and talking to their neighbors every day. This campaign was built by grassroots supporters from New Hampshire and across the country, and all of you will decide this race in these final 12 days.
Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and a network of special interest donors have spent over $64 million trying to buy this seat for John Sununu. They're betting that their millions can drown out the voices of the people of New Hampshire. We're betting on you.
**The other side has millions in outside spending. We have you.**
**[Will you chip in $15 today to help us win New Hampshire and flip the Senate in 12 days?](https://substack.com/redirect/fd95e8d9-ce8e-4566-9d12-3652a050475f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/fd95e8d9-ce8e-4566-9d12-3652a050475f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_If you couldn 't be there on Saturday, here's the full transcript of my remarks:_
* * *
Good afternoon, Exeter.
Thanks, everyone, for joining this great event today. I want to thank Senator Hassan for your introduction and your comments, and most importantly, for the leadership that you're providing for the people of New Hampshire right now.
This is not a time to stand down. It's a time to stand up. And if you've watched Maggie Hassan in action over the last couple of years in Washington, she is standing up for the people of New Hampshire every day. Thank you for your leadership.
And what a great day when we can join our next Congresswoman, Stefany Shaheen, and our next Governor, Cinde Warmington. Thank you for being out here, guys. I know it's been a long day.
It's another No Kings Day. Happy No Kings Day, everyone.
This is the original No Kings state. You heard a little bit about the history right here in Exeter 250 years ago when we inked independence into the fabric of who we are as Granite Staters. We didn't stand for kings then, and we're not about to start doing that in 2026, are we?
I've got members of my family here. My amazing mom and my husband Vann are here. This is an all-hands-on-deck team effort. We need everyone under the tent.
This week we announced a list of endorsers for our campaign who are putting country over party. We are building a big tent, because it's not just about bringing together progressives and moderate Democrats. It's about bringing together independents and Republicans who are sick and tired of what's going on in this nation, who know that this is not as good as it gets for the United States of America.
**Together we can write a chapter and build a future that is fairer and freer for every Granite Stater, and everyone has a stake in that future.**
We're really proud of the support that we are building, and it includes all of you from every single corner of this state.
We've got to get out there and do the work these next 17 days, because everything is on the line. This is the most important midterm election of our lifetime, because we have a government and a reckless, incompetent president who is out of control.
You can count on one hand the number of Republicans that are actually standing up and doing something about it. That caucus of capitulation and cowardice has far too many members in Washington, D.C. right now. And despite some showing occasional concern, we can't send a Senator from New Hampshire who is going to capitulate and cower to Donald Trump. We need someone who's going to put the people of this state first.
John Sununu has said as much. He says that this race is "important to Donald Trump's agenda" and to protecting the successes of the Trump Administration. Now I don't know what those successes are. Do you?
Is it $4.50 gas? Is it record diesel costs? Is it the $1,000 that you just put in your home heating oil tank? Is it the fact that tens of thousands of Granite Staters are losing health care? Is it the tariffs that are hammering our small businesses? What are those successes?
John Sununu sounds a lot like Trump, who proclaims this to be a golden age for America. Are you buying that? The people of New Hampshire aren't buying it.
It might be a golden age if you're Don Jr. and a Russian oligarch is paying for your wedding reception. It might be a golden age if you're the pool guy who just got a no-bid contract to do the reflecting pool. It might be a golden age if you're getting special treatment and you're part of the Epstein class. And it might be a golden age if you're Donald Trump himself, who's $2.2 billion richer than when he came into the White House in January of last year.
The corruption is out in the open right now, and people like John Sununu are turning a blind eye to it. They're sidling up to Donald Trump on all the policies that are making life worse: the way our economy is being rigged for those at the top and the way our political system is being flooded with all this out-of-state money because they think that their millions are more powerful than your voice.
**But here in New Hampshire, we 're going to say something pretty profound this year: Our votes are not for sale.**
This is still the Live Free or Die state, and we have the power in our own hands to decide what comes next in this country.
We get to decide that we're not just going to blindly follow Donald Trump's agenda. We get to stand up and fight for people in New Hampshire who deserve a better future. We get to fight to make sure we're delivering health care as a right, and not a privilege, to every Granite Stater. We're fighting hard to get big money out of our political system, end partisan gerrymandering, and put the power of our democracy in your hands.
We have the power to determine how we protect our air and our water and act to protect this planet and take action on climate change. We have the power to bring down costs and make sure that there's opportunity for families who are struggling and sturdy rungs on the ladder of opportunity for future generations.
We have the power to build a strong system of public education and take on those that are siphoning money out of our public schools. We have the power to protect the personal freedoms of everyone, especially women who have been subject to draconian laws all across this country that are taking away their right to choose. We can restore _Roe v. Wade_ if we reassert our political power this year.
There's so much that we can accomplish.
I had two debates this week with John Sununu. In one of them, he said that he wasn't going to tell you what his plans were for Social Security because he was afraid he was going to get attacked in the campaign for them. Probably means he wants to cut benefits, right? Probably means he would entertain cutting benefits or raising the retirement age. But I have to tell you this: I am fighting to preserve Social Security and make sure that it's there for today's seniors and tomorrow's retirees.
This election is about how we muster the courage we need to stand up to a broken presidency, how we stand up to the billionaire class and the corporate special interests that are calling all the shots in Washington, D.C. right now, and how we write that next chapter for the future of New Hampshire and for this nation.
It's about turning the page on Trump and turning the page on the broken politics of the past that are reflected by John Sununu.
I don't have to remind you all that he was our Senator before. Many of you remember that. It didn't end well for New Hampshire. He was down the line for George W. Bush. He supported forever wars. He supported massive tax breaks to the super-wealthy and the biggest corporations that added trillions of dollars to our debt. He supported a $700 billion bailout of Wall Street while Main Street got screwed during the housing crisis. He voted to put anti-choice judges on the bench who overturned _Roe v. Wade_.
We've seen the movie before. We know the sequel is always worse. Why would we walk into the theater again and buy a ticket to see the show?
We've got to turn the page on John Sununu and the broken politics of the past, because this is about what comes next. We need a new generation of leadership in the United States Senate, and I'm fighting to be that Senator from New Hampshire.
These guys are flooding the zone with their dark money. We see it every day. It's on all of your screens, and it's coming from Donald Trump's super PAC, from Elon Musk, from the Koch network, literally spending over $64 million already and counting on this race.
But we've got something pretty profound to talk about here. It's a message about the future. It's a message about hope. It's a message about inclusion. It's a message about a fair economy. And we're going to work hard the next 17 days to deliver that message.
We need your help to get it out. So sign up for a canvass shift, make some phone calls, talk to your neighbors about the stakes in this election.
We have come so far over the last year and a half, at a moment where Trump wasn't counting on this sort of response from the American public. He thought we would be so overwhelmed that we would back off of our responsibilities as citizens, that we would just relinquish our vote, our power to speak out and push back.
This is a time not to fold. It's time to continue to fight and do what you have done on No Kings Day, at the protest in Merrimack, New Hampshire, to stop that ICE facility from being built, and in special elections where we've been picking up steam in towns and cities across New Hampshire. We are on the march. We have to sustain this effort over the next 17 days to get the kind of representation that we deserve in Washington, D.C.
This is a tough fight, but we can absolutely win it. Let's continue to link arms. Let's continue to work hard.
At the beginning of Trump 2.0, there were a lot of Democrats saying, "Well just ride it out, and you'll have a good midterm in a couple of years." That doesn't work for people who are being harmed by the policies of this government. It doesn't work for our federal workforce that is being drummed out of service with the DOGE cuts. It doesn't work for New Hampshire families who are losing access to health care. It doesn't work for people who care about the strength of American democracy.
Governor Newsom showed us how to stand up and fight back, not with one hand tied behind our back, but by trying to find every point of leverage that we have to make the case and to hold the line for democracy and Americans who are counting on us.
We've got to continue to muster that courage over the next 17 days. If we follow that example, we're going to win here. We're going to elect candidates up and down the ticket. We're going to turn New Hampshire blue from top to bottom, and we're going to flip the majorities, not just in Concord, but in the House and Senate in Washington and begin to unwind the damage that's been caused to our democracy.
Let's get out there and do it. Let's keep fighting. Let's win this. Let's deliver the kind of future that New Hampshire deserves.
I'd be honored to be your Senator. Let's work to make it happen.
Thank you so much. Thanks for being here.

**It’s time for something different.** This grassroots movement is gearing up to retire Sen. Marshall once and for all and end the chaos and corruption in Washington.

## Russia Frees Jailed American Teacher
Russia [freed a retired teacher](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAQhp_GbI6OMyF48NCFLV07IgeOcJWxkX0kSp--In2Ebied_k__939dh6vnwPH-6VdyMqch0rMEEqE85L0U9nMmKn6lzKOPk493ygMCtroGjTj4UfhBQ11NbiZCMhW5-mKxbc8Aplpca8zYYWMJrQdrrO-QADtjmu4Ms4WK3YGrAbEGAwAn8tTasW1gtNjNl0Y1QBNLyqfvxFEWmsMrPSifxrRWwS0iW1HmQ2GvsI-vLRU5Xgr7A6ywr-G4a4X9M-Uw6cNRYf_np9-Cmtctc0mRJr0XPbLwD0VdhLaFol72283nSftZKOst0BFLq5a8r5vCvspu2p4cApf2ohq4r57Du5_8b9WHw98AAAD__4QFi84) from Michigan on Wednesday after holding him for more than four years. Stephen Hubbard, 74, was seized in Ukraine in 2022 and later sentenced on a mercenary charge his family denies. President Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin released Hubbard at his request, with "no 'swap' necessary." Hubbard, who is in poor health, is [headed to Texas](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFutDAQBeDTmM5oGPiBLVz8Dd2mTYnGZrxMFgyyzaLcPiJRTpBupJGe3vfe7-OdZJHweKOVTfbbGPhMC-fMcYxHSkI-MidaOYqjMFF4cBwRsNUVaMSRXJYXj1UxGc-MXBdsqu6GbfsPoC5m07saa_KTdbb3XcXO2pb6DnpbV8C-KcRccRUgVlADQMnE7c21Dbgb9r5rVAM8Sd5i-bFJyDP75XN7cSzdthaLmXPek6r_KxwUDud5ls6mi3H9FQ7XqXD40eiUeZ856PmwluKkL96kf336eEaSwPqkqE_Jz817vR9ZgsKhiGbaT1kWSW2nGnisJMt3ify36V4GvwIAAP__2UqGPw) for treatment at a military hospital. U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff, in St. Petersburg for talks with Putin, called the Russian leader "a humanitarian," [drawing criticism from](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O2zAQRk9DdTLIkUJJBYs06jZtSmGWGpqT5Y9BjmXk9oFzha0_4Ht47_fH8YGcuNx_YSYnoR6FXj2RCLWjPXtnDI2oY6bGHsuJ5U7tAA12NHoEONALX3SY4XSBCGgayJllA2t_aD0N0Vkz-XMCEwxt24rzppcJPJp1_QyrRRjYve-MBjB60lrfCMlu3s7ab7CGZVazppOlttufykUihfS3XtRuvuYhuSjy6Gr6qWBXsEukyCm9NwV7rJneRgp2PDMX7tJQuBYFuzUWJmPHLnTR-GL5qiGMV8KTM7fx8RQuY3xmLCzYGMv4if4rYY8K9qG58_HilLjbRc36npH_Qwf5XsbLwb8AAAD__2zwiJs) some Republicans. North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis called the remark "embarrassing and outrageous." Hubbard was the last American the U.S. [formally deemed wrongfully detained](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ8GOqNl4eBcuPib6-5vU6LFXg7njEFrcyhvH5EoeYF0oxlpNN-83Yc7-eDj4z8tbPK0DpGPFDhnlkH2lDxNwpxoYfGWoqP4YBkQsFM1KMSBbPYvHurSmYkZuSnZ1L3GrrsANOVsyHLTX1jr9krIeK11QyPpqR7hAtrp0puzrgbEGhoAqJi407ZrwWq8Tn1btMDO51Wq99XHPPMUPtYXS2XXpQxmznlLRfOvwFuBt-M4qjjaE-PMT2eV4Aq8feP8CiUcmBI79QOnUuZt5qjmfRxJnMqyL5va9uyj2p9CPrI6SFSm8ExKbKQO2r6BUozbDh-CT11ftPBYyIevdflvn74MfgYAAP__jxWOWw) in Russia. The Kremlin says three-way peace talks with the U.S. and Ukraine could resume in mid-November.
## Chemical Explosion Forces Toledo Evacuations
A [chemical tank explosion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOnTAURL8GOj9dLjyzFC7S0G3alOiuPTwcGfvJNqD8fUSUP9juSCONZs6vz-VTfPDx9VN2mLqmJeIqAbUiL_koxcuagSI7srcSncQX8sLEWnWkmBex1Z9YutaZFWD0LUw3Tqz1k6hvN2OZRzd1kC8nMtiVnutEjPH5QbpjPbbe3HUdMXfUE9EDAj1ZPZCd-GMdh2YgOF9TfvxOPtYNa_iTTuSHTXsbzFbruzT9j4bnhufruh7xy9437rzh-caG56Oo_4RT7CHVp1hU2RAqsnoHsVApO-SifCkHnKopwCWVNp-U3bB7K0FlBEiByjaKpmHspzYb9758CL7osRnotYsP_7bV7xk9Df8NAAD__0EBjVQ) in Toledo, Ohio, on Tuesday night forced nearly 1,000 residents from their homes. Officials also ordered everyone within 3 miles to shelter in place with windows shut. The 5,500-gallon tank at a chemical transport terminal held glycidyl methacrylate, a chemical [used to make plastics](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQAL_GdEbL4jNQuEhDd2lToo1Zjk2MfbJ9cPn76N4vvHqk0Wh-3Zc7SZD4-EkHu7qlJfJVAtfKecmvUoS2zFzo4Cye4krxwXlBQKs70IgL-SonL12zuo0ZuW_YdcOE1t4A-mZ3628czdR5exto4rWnzXbjZKcbDNtowTbiProOEDvoAaBlYjt5a8BPOG6DUQZ4lZpy-ydJrDtv4V86Obc-HU1we63PovofCmeF83Vd7VWJP1DhTLmKD6xwrinwmrTf-RBPQVeKfzW_nyEVSVHX9BavMwemwppP8i-qkmJROA8GwRiAJrv1eUkIUuygDDwOkvBVUb_37nT4PwAA__-Nm4QX) and paints. Hazmat crews stayed back overnight because of the risk of another blast. About 35 people were [treated at local hospitals](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2SozAQhU8jMqimAWEFCjZR5k03pNpSy2hLIJckm_GcfoqZI0zUHbz63s-_63KlEMN-_0sb6-rTsvNRItfKecnPUgL5zFxo4xws7Y72O-cFAWXbQ4u4kK3hxUvfOO2ZkYeGdT8rlHICGJpVW7xNHi7OT_M0eKVug5OgnJuBZ3sbL03QJ64HxB4GAOiYWCorR7AKL34exQjsQk25-5_CXlf28Z1enDubtibqtdZHEcMfgUagOY6jexaqydH7FAg0pab8FmjOauehGtIu0Jy2Ak0P598LNDVFdqld6ZOyS8_SblQ5B4qltStvwVJs-eMRU_kBKBwmBaMEmAWaJmv3OEKMochZjHDfKMTvjPV3y740fgUAAP__fjSL7w) for symptoms possibly tied to the release, and a sheriff’s deputy was injured. Toledo Public Schools closed all 57 of its schools Wednesday. The Ohio Environmental Protection Agency blamed an “error” during a transfer of the chemical. Dear Pro-Life Friend,

Our volunteer student canvassers have been through the wringer these past couple of months.

Doors get slammed in their faces. They get shouted off stoops. And sometimes, even worse things happen.

So, I’ve told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two weeks.

Pro-Life Friend, our student canvassers know what’s on the line.

They know if abortion-loving leftists seize power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

And they know the job’s not done yet.

But right now, they could use a little moral boost heading into the final weeks before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3rd.

[That’s why I’m hoping you’ll prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L-K3DAQx_Gnkbs11siW7woVgWW7S5vSzEojrTj9QxpfyNsHh-QF0kzzheHD78fH8YExxRK-YybT2R99HPyiX50CMccSXK19jIQ5kztgAX2Tyw3gQMvxi44VJ2ecdSjtREbu76D1tqxyehklUdlt2_zT2ze9u402qzYlnb8OwBTN9U8uAHJRi3qbcfc7qSfsK0m7wVOsCybqPHdq5zNFi4VxfPraLc225imZF3MbQn0T8BDwGGTPTvPg01Hh4WtP0dNFrWWuPQh4NLxZ7NTQfmIg0EI9RrdC3Sm3LkDnEaIT6n7B5HtDAfrkfFjMDWMoV_mL_ldqYSos1L2zn7px7WdMKQ69i3UJGWP6Q-X_XPfLwO8AAAD___fci3A)**.**

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

These young women and men will be on their feet for hours, walking door to door. And knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going.

Of course, I could tell our door knockers to go home.

I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead.

But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad ever could. And the effect doesn’t disappear after one election.

**Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote again in the next election, too.**

And, it costs us less than $3 for every door we knock.

This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that’s needed to turn out every pro-life voter.

Last cycle, this approach worked.
**> >> In Oklahoma,** our canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion state senators who killed our legislation to stop chemical abortion pill trafficking. Voters threw them out.

**> >> In South Carolina,** we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who killed our “Life at Conception Act.” They lost too.

**> >> In North Carolina,** 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries.
The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to give up and go home during this final stretch.

It’s true they have the money, the media, and the institutions.

But what they don’t have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger’s door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words, and still go knock on the next door.

That grit and determination is what wins elections.

[So, will you please make your most generous contribution today to keep our canvassers in the field through the two most important weeks of this election season](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L-K3DAQx_Gnkbs11siW7woVgWW7S5vSzEojrTj9QxpfyNsHh-QF0kzzheHD78fH8YExxRK-YybT2R99HPyiX50CMccSXK19jIQ5kztgAX2Tyw3gQMvxi44VJ2ecdSjtREbu76D1tqxyehklUdlt2_zT2ze9u402qzYlnb8OwBTN9U8uAHJRi3qbcfc7qSfsK0m7wVOsCybqPHdq5zNFi4VxfPraLc225imZF3MbQn0T8BDwGGTPTvPg01Hh4WtP0dNFrWWuPQh4NLxZ7NTQfmIg0EI9RrdC3Sm3LkDnEaIT6n7B5HtDAfrkfFjMDWMoV_mL_ldqYSos1L2zn7px7WdMKQ69i3UJGWP6Q-X_XPfLwO8AAAD___fci3A)**?**

**> >> $25** pays for a canvasser’s meals for a day in the field.

**> >> $10** puts our pro-life message on more than three doors.
Pro-Life Friend, door knocking has been our key to beating both the Abortion Lobby and the D.C. consultant class for years.

You see, they like wasting their donors’ money on flashy, expensive cable TV ads because it lines their pockets.

Meanwhile, real people having real conversations are what actually move voters in November. That’s how we helped 119 pro-life legislators WIN in 2024!

So, please let our dedicated student activists know you care about them and appreciate the hard work they’re doing for the entire pro-life movement.

Dear Peter, In America, the people choose their government. And the people deserve to know their choices have been accurately recorded and counted. Elections must be conducted according to the law, with transparency and reliable records to prove the results. As another national election approaches, questions about public confidence remain. At Unite4Freedom, our optimism is grounded in something tangible:**we understand the problem, we have a strategy, and we are making progress.** In addition to **State Scorecards in 35 states** and **Vote Tampering Reports in 10 states** , consider what we've accomplished this year:
* Volunteers used Unite4Freedom's data analysis to file administrative complaints in 5 states, pursue formal hearings concerning compliance with federal election requirements and citizens' right to be heard, and achieve **on-the-record hearings in Missouri, Colorado, and Illinois.**
* Unite4Freedom issued **formal notices to 30 states** about potential violations of federal voter registration requirements. We maintain that the states' responses have not fully addressed or reconciled those concerns, providing **a basis for further legal action.**
* Unite4Freedom issued **preservation notices to 35 states** ahead of election-record retention deadlines, requesting that records be preserved and notifying officials of potential civil litigation if violations are not corrected.
* Our Pennsylvania lawsuit **survived a motion to dismiss** , allowing us to continue pursuing our claims in court. We are preparing additional federal litigation based on our previously listed complaints and analysis.

**Our work doesn't end on Election Day.** These accomplishments are part of a long-term strategy to document concerns, obtain on-the-record review, and pursue accountability through established legal processes. Meaningful reform takes time. Unite4Freedom remains committed to examining election records, seeking answers, and pursuing legal remedies beyond this election. **Will you help us continue this work with a donation today?**

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I’m not going to sugarcoat this
body:
We were almost there. We can still win this.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I want to be straight with you, because you’ve earned that.
Back in April, I was down almost 7 points to Greg Abbott in the polling average. Political insiders wrote this race off. Then you showed up: you chipped in, spread the word, and proved that people all over the country believe Texas can be taken back. **By October 7, we had cut that gap to just 1.3 points.**
I know a lot of you saw that number and felt what I felt: _we can actually do this._
But since then, the polls have moved in the wrong direction. Today, the average has me trailing Abbott by 2.4 points.
Here’s what I need you to hear:**2.4 points is not a lost race.** This is one of the most competitive governor’s races in the country, and it will be decided by turnout, by organizing, and by what we do in these final days.

Two weeks ago, we were closer to beating Greg Abbott than anyone thought possible. If we let up now, we could lose this race by a margin we could have closed. [**I need you in this fight with me. Can you chip in $15 today to help us get back to where we were and finish the job?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261022_1_pollslipped.7O9mka&refcode=emrefcode%3Dem20261022-mailing_id&amount=15&t=2&akid=2500%2E299639%2E1HxzFv)
Early voting is already underway, and every dollar we raise right now goes straight into reaching the voters who will decide this thing. We can’t get comfortable. Not for a single day. **We have to make sure every voter hears the truth about Greg Abbott before they cast their ballot.**
Here’s just one example: yesterday, a watchdog investigation found that Abbott’s much-hyped “pause” on data center permits was never a pause at all. Dozens of projects kept moving forward. That’s Greg Abbott: a press release for voters, business as usual for his corporate allies.
_**Your donation could be the difference between winning and losing.**_ It could decide whether Texas gets four more years of Greg Abbott’s corruption or whether we take Texas back.
I’ve never needed your support more. [**Will you chip in $15 now so we can close this 2.4-point gap before Election Day?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20261022_1_pollslipped.cBTQVO&refcode=em20261022-2500&t=4&akid=2500%2E299639%2E1HxzFv)
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261022_1_pollslipped.Yhe3Q5&refcode=em20261022-2500&t=23&akid=2500%2E299639%2E1HxzFv)
We closed a 7-point gap once already. Two points is within reach, but it’s now or never, and I need you with me today.
Thank you,
Gina
_Our records aren’t perfect – if you’ve donated with a different email address, phone number, or by check, not all of your gifts may be reflected in our accounting here. Our team greatly appreciates all of your support in electing me as the next Governor of Texas!_

# Thursday, October 22, 2026
---|---
**Good Morning!** On this day in 1836, Sam Houston [took the oath](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uhDAQxfHTmA5kZvmwCxdp6DZtSjS2BxjJi1d4xG5uH4UcIf1fPz29r_t8R068r5_4ICfvJc87vUoiETpmoTeWBXeP-04RhWjHlbCUGTQMdatrgBmD8Elzh1V0XkfbVuTa0cIwDNbYanO-84CLNSYS2nE0FAP1oBftb54gxIrdL9dqgLbVN22asHR9Z_TQGx96NFZ1miJLPhrZ6G9U-s4nHU3Ijyq5TeRZ1O1DwaRgki00V9Ss-VQwbVwkHxzqwkJFwbTwUaQO-GTJqb7S6nDx-eKUuAyj6vT6QE6XLv995XTwEwAA__85T3ld) as the Republic of Texas' first elected president in Columbia, now West Columbia. Interim President David Burnet resigned without warning, leaving Houston two hours to write his inaugural address. Your milk says it expired seven days ago. | | Dear Fellow American, Something deeply troubling is happening in America, and it’s happening faster than most people realize. Last year, New York City’s socialist mayor said he wanted to replace what he called **“the frigidity of rugged individualism” with “the warmth of collectivism.”** Then I read that a senior official in that same administration argued that private property is a tool of **oppression**. Those statements are troubling enough. But what really stopped me in my tracks was hearing a popular socialist podcaster tell his audience to **“Kill... landlords... Let the streets soak in their...****capitalist blood.****”** How on earth did ideas like these become acceptable, even helping far-Left candidates to win elections from coast to coast? body:
Illegal Votes, Turnout, and the Partisan Divide

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-october-8-12775790?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/msYv6Jrfy3w?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)
| | **Illegal Votes, Turnout, and the Partisan Divide** By Jeffrey Milyo, Professor of Economics, University of MissouriThe policy debate over voting rules such as voter ID, drop boxes for ballots, or vote-by-mail may be understood as disagreements about the relative importance of making it easier for eligible citizens to vote versus preventing ineligible people from doing so. The parties have staked out widely divergent positions on specific reforms, but where does the American public stand when it comes to prioritizing one goal over the other?As part of my ongoing research on election administration and with recent support from the Grant Institute, I have collected survey data on public knowledge and opinions of state election procedures over several years. A total of twelve national surveys between 2008 and 2024 asked respondents whether the more important priority for their state should be “maximizing voter turnout even if some illegal voting occurs, or minimizing illegal voting even if that reduces turnout.”Over the entire period (N>11,000), Americans chose minimizing illegal voting over increasing turnout by a margin of more than two to one. Among those identifying most strongly with the Republican Party, the ratio exceeds ten to one, and among those who lean toward neither party the ratio is about 4.6 to one. In contrast, among strong Democrats the balance tips the other way, by about 1.5 to one in favor of increasing turnout. These ratios are also stable across years, although there is some evidence of increased polarization in 2024.These findings raise the question of whether the partisan divide reflects different views of the trade-offs or cues from party leaders. In a new study with David Doherty, Conor Dowling, and Michael Miller, I address this with two survey experiments conducted in 2024. Respondents chose between two voting rules for a hypothetical town. Under one, every eligible resident voted, but so did some ineligible residents; under the other, no ineligible residents voted, but fewer eligible residents did. We randomly varied the numbers on each side, as well as which party was said to have proposed each rule.Respondents in these experiments treated an illegal vote as far weightier than a lost legal one, giving roughly as much weight to one ineligible ballot as to ten eligible citizens not voting, and Democrats and Republicans responded to these trade-offs in much the same way, although Republicans were 18 to 19 percentage points more likely to favor eliminating illegal votes. Party cues, however, had enormous effects: support for the rule that eliminated illegal voting rose by 37 to 48 percentage points when it was attributed to the respondent’s own party.These findings suggest that much of the partisan conflict over voting rules reflects signals from party leaders rather than fundamentally different values. Americans across the political spectrum place a high priority on keeping ineligible votes out of elections, which leaves more room for compromise than the current debate would suggest.Professor Milyo’s article, coauthored with David Doherty, Conor M. Dowling, and Michael G. Miller, is available [here](https://us.list-manage.com/c0Hf_wxrg3c?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)._Professor Milyo’s work was funded in part by the Ulysses S. Grant Institute. The views expressed by the author are his own and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Institute._

| | **Arizona** The Maricopa County Recorder’s Office [reported](https://us.list-manage.com/18ulMssKI1k?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) unauthorized overnight access to the paper trays of three ballot-on-demand printers at an early voting site at Chandler-Gilbert Community College. The office replaced the printers and sent them for forensic examination. No voters were affected.Attorney General Mayes’s office [demanded](https://us.list-manage.com/12_dev4Amvj?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in a letter to Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap that he restore 24 voters the county attorney’s investigation found to be U.S. citizens from “Not Eligible” to active or inactive status. The letter stated the office is prepared to seek mandamus this week if he does not.**California** California voters will decide November 3 on Proposition 39, an initiative constitutional amendment that would [require](https://us.list-manage.com/c8DUWZv7IUU?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) government-issued identification to vote in person. The measure additionally would invalidate mail ballots lacking the last four digits of an ID number designated in the voter’s registration, and direct election officials to verify registrants’ citizenship with government data and report each county’s verification rate annually.The Riverside County Registrar of Voters [scheduled the destruction](https://us.list-manage.com/B4bTbMUJRnZ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of the roughly 650,000 November 2025 special election ballots returned by the sheriff, after the Secretary of State’s office advised that state law required it.Shasta County [left](https://us.list-manage.com/ByIZrRgd6ch?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the Redding city clerk race off November ballots. A county supervisor said the omission could require a special election costing $200,000 to $300,000.Twelve unvoted San Diego County mail ballots were [found](https://us.list-manage.com/ONr_IhGYO67?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) along a road outside Escondido. The Registrar of Voters said it found no sign of fraud or of loss in its custody and was working with the Postal Service to trace them.Humboldt County [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/nYvmCAQdI85?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) voter information guides missing the statements of two local candidates. The county sent affected voters the statements with a letter explaining the error.Tulare County’s print vendor [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/uKd3PjDXn5q?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) duplicate vote-by-mail ballots to 7,791 voters in the city of Tulare. The registrar said any second ballot returned will be rejected.Federal agents [arrested](https://us.list-manage.com/gAlLrNFbxuG?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) noncitizens for registering and voting in federal elections in a statewide operation that charged 28 lawful permanent residents across California’s four federal districts, including a Belizean national accused of voting in 2020, 2022, and 2024.An unknown number of mail ballots were [stolen](https://us.list-manage.com/7kPp3SbD5CQ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) from a Daly City post office. San Mateo County election officials directed affected voters to request replacements while the Postal Inspection Service investigates.An Orange County prosecution of a Costa Mesa woman who registered her dog to vote and cast its ballot in the 2021 recall [ended in dismissal](https://us.list-manage.com/kW9T2qpGNXX?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) after she completed a plea agreement that required her to pay $1,500 for four anti-voter-fraud billboards.The Imperial County Registrar of Voters [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/dTqwyvBgdcU?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an extra ballot to about 160 confidential voters while changing its procedures for elected officials and candidates newly eligible for confidential status. Only one ballot per voter will be counted.**Colorado** About 835,000 voters in Adams, Arapahoe, Douglas, and Weld counties [received](https://us.list-manage.com/zFnvpysj7Yn?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) ballots carrying Issue 7A, a Front Range Passenger Rail District sales tax question, because the district did not tell county clerks the legislature had narrowed its boundaries. Counties will leave wholly ineligible precincts out of the 7A results and separate eligible ballots by hand in split precincts.Some Pueblo County residents, most in the Rye Fire District, [received](https://us.list-manage.com/1C2t91ZIwgP?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a second ballot carrying only special district tax questions. The clerk’s office attributed the error to inaccurate voter lists supplied by the districts.**District of Columbia** The D.C. Board of Elections [asked](https://us.list-manage.com/5KCzgJ00ltn?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the National Guard to limit where its members are posted near drop boxes and voting sites after troops were seen beside a Foggy Bottom drop box. Joint Task Force-DC said its members are directed not to monitor or secure polling locations.**Florida** The Florida Department of Law Enforcement [arrested](https://us.list-manage.com/uSFn46VJfEV?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a Palm Beach County man convicted of second-degree murder in 1998, whose voting rights were never restored, on two counts of false affirmation on voter registration applications and one count of voting as an unqualified elector.The Monroe County Supervisor of Elections [replaced](https://us.list-manage.com/uar3XJTSwMI?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the tabulators and electronic voter identification systems at the Big Pine Key early voting site after a resident found the building unlocked with the equipment unattended two days before early voting began. Officials said the equipment had not been tampered with.**Georgia** The Athens-Clarke County Elections Department [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/7ASt3HY6BSO?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a second absentee ballot to 1,154 voters after overlapping address lists went to its print vendor. The department said only one ballot per voter will be accepted.Poll workers [began handwriting](https://us.list-manage.com/166otJjO3Ri?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) each early voter’s name on a numbered list under a State Election Board rule that creates a paper record of who voted.**Illinois** Kendall County [sent](https://us.list-manage.com/8c2KkeTaszp?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 300 mail ballots to two precincts carrying a referendum those voters were not eligible to decide, then spoiled and reissued them.**Indiana** Floyd County [left](https://us.list-manage.com/tt265TQD_0Y?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the District 1 county commissioner race off the early in-person and absentee ballots of 572 voters in four precincts because of a programming error. The county said affected voters will be able to cast corrected ballots.**Iowa** Warren County [sent](https://us.list-manage.com/IQr6OnQagvK?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an extra absentee ballot to 613 voters, and Secretary of State Paul Pate said safeguards will ensure only one ballot from each is counted.**Kentucky** Caldwell County [printed](https://us.list-manage.com/ubGLsrk34NY?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the two candidates in a school board race in reverse of their drawn order. The clerk had vendor Harp Enterprises reprint the ballots after five absentee ballots had gone out.**Massachusetts** Some of the roughly 280 Pelham mail ballot packets [went out](https://us.list-manage.com/lvWuBfeO__d?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) with two copies of page one and no page two, which carries the last two referendum questions. The town clerk attributed the error to the vendor the Secretary of the Commonwealth hired to assemble the packets.The Cambridge Election Commission [warned](https://us.list-manage.com/znbcrVUemgs?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that some of its pre-assembled mail ballot packets, also supplied by the Commonwealth, contained the same error.**Michigan** Tuscarora Township [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/v48Qutao7W9?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) its absentee ballots more than a week after the statutory 40-day deadline. The deputy clerk apologized after the ACLU of Michigan threatened legal action.The Wayne County Board of Canvassers [counted](https://us.list-manage.com/UiVykRjsDTb?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 37 absentee ballots excluded from Hamtramck’s 2025 mayoral count under a final court order, reversing the result. Certification is on hold pending a separate challenge to the winner’s residency.**Nevada** The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada [announced](https://us.list-manage.com/OfYUZyi8hBS?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an election integrity plan for early voting and Election Day.**New York** Monroe County’s mail ballot vendor [delayed](https://us.list-manage.com/11DC5GhtWZo?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) part of a batch of about 7,000 ballots because it lacked enough of the correct envelopes. County election commissioners said the remaining ballots have since been mailed.**North Carolina** Gov. Josh Stein [urged](https://us.list-manage.com/poYGcWcMxiu?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) voters to vote in person, citing an advocacy group’s analysis of 27 counties that found about 3% of mail ballots rejected so far, double the 2022 rate.**Oklahoma** The state’s online voter registration system [failed](https://us.list-manage.com/QZdM0RwF2Ia?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) for a couple of hours on the afternoon of the registration deadline because of a communication problem with Service Oklahoma’s data. The State Election Board did not extend the deadline.**Pennsylvania** Dauphin County [rejected](https://us.list-manage.com/B2CkADxFQoq?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 10 mail ballot applications bearing repeated signatures and other irregularities. The district attorney’s investigation identified a person tied to a get-out-the-vote group who admitted falsifying them.Berks County’s mail ballots were [delayed](https://us.list-manage.com/M8RSiBzXKXF?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) by an envelope supply problem at the county’s printing vendor.**Tennessee** The DeKalb County Sheriff’s Department [charged](https://us.list-manage.com/o61yA5emqa1?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Alexandria’s town recorder and court clerk with illegal registration or voting for allegedly denying a 2011 felony conviction on a June registration form and voting in the August election.**Texas** Counties [cleared](https://us.list-manage.com/15_kr1yF4xq?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the backlog of more than 500,000 voter registration records the Department of Public Safety had failed to transmit, according to the Secretary of State’s office. The office said affected registrants missing from the rolls may vote provisional ballots that will be counted.The Secretary of State’s office and its vendor Civix [re-sent](https://us.list-manage.com/122tvTGMH9I?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) counties about 15,000 online address updates submitted since September 1 that an extra address validation had held back. The office then sent some files again after counties found them missing the updated addresses.Nearly 1.8 million registrants, more than 9% of the state’s 19 million, [were on](https://us.list-manage.com/15Dz4jtdr5F?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the suspense list in figures the Secretary of State’s office released before early voting. Suspense voters who moved to another county may cast limited ballots only during early voting.**Utah** About 4,300 voters [received](https://us.list-manage.com/vege06fQ8lj?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) federal-only ballots because their citizenship could not yet be verified under HB 209’s documentary proof requirement for state and local races. They can obtain full ballots by verifying citizenship by October 23.**Virginia** Gov. Abigail Spanberger [said](https://us.list-manage.com/JEXgfXeGl7a?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) her administration is investigating why rights-restoration letters, which link recipients to voter registration, were sent to deceased Virginians.Attorney General Jay Jones [created](https://us.list-manage.com/Yiropxt0Kc9?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a “Voter Protection Section” to investigate improper registration cancellations, absentee ballot denials, and voter intimidation and to enforce the Virginia Voting Rights Act.
---
|
---
| | **Oregon** Oregon Motor Voter ProgramComment deadline: November 10, 2026The Secretary of State [proposed amending OAR 165-005-0170](https://us.list-manage.com/s48AnY9zoPl?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a). The Secretary states the rule “replaces the previously adopted Oregon Motor Voter Registration Manual.” The “changes include notifications to qualified individuals during a covered transaction at DMV that their information is being sent to SoS for voter registration purposes, requiring OMV materials to be produced in multiple languages, updating contents of OMV notification mailed to registrants, updating the timing of [Oregon Motor Voter] data transfer from SoS to county election officials, updating processing instructions for county election officials, and requiring DMV and SoS to enter into an interagency agreement detailing file transfer specifications, daily control file policies, monthly audits, and SoS initiated list maintenance procedures.”
---
|
---
| | **Federal Agencies** _**Federal Communications Commission v. Brown**_**, No. 26-2230 (4th Cir.)** On October 14, the U.S. Supreme Court [stayed](https://us.list-manage.com/Zs9EOU4O6qM?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the Fourth Circuit’s October 7 mandamus order directing the Federal Communications Commission to rule within 48 hours on candidates’ challenge to its guidance that joint fundraising committees and coordinated political parties are entitled to broadcasters’ lowest unit charge. The Court reasoned that the Communications Act does not require the Commission to act on such applications within a particular timeframe.**Alabama** _**Alabama State Conference of the NAACP v. Attorney General of Alabama**_ , **No. 2:24-cv-00420 (N.D. Ala.)** On October 14, the Supreme Court of Alabama [heard argument](https://us.list-manage.com/SJ3Ggq5rf6Z?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) on questions certified by the Eleventh Circuit about the reach of SB 1’s payment and gift provisions on absentee-ballot application assistance. clean_body: Illegal Votes, Turnout, and the Partisan Divide | | | | | | | | | Illegal Votes, Turnout, and the Partisan Divide By Jeffrey Milyo, Professor of Economics, University of MissouriThe policy debate over voting rules such as voter ID, drop boxes for ballots, or vote-by-mail may be understood as disagreements about the relative importance of making it easier for eligible citizens to vote versus preventing ineligible people from doing so. The parties have staked out widely divergent positions on specific reforms, but where does the American public stand when it comes to prioritizing one goal over the other?As part of my ongoing research on election administration and with recent support from the Grant Institute, I have collected survey data on public knowledge and opinions of state election procedures over several years. A total of twelve national surveys between 2008 and 2024 asked respondents whether the more important priority for their state should be “maximizing voter turnout even if some illegal voting occurs, or minimizing illegal voting even if that reduces turnout.”Over the entire period (N>11,000), Americans chose minimizing illegal voting over increasing turnout by a margin of more than two to one. Among those identifying most strongly with the Republican Party, the ratio exceeds ten to one, and among those who lean toward neither party the ratio is about 4.6 to one. In contrast, among strong Democrats the balance tips the other way, by about 1.5 to one in favor of increasing turnout. These ratios are also stable across years, although there is some evidence of increased polarization in 2024.These findings raise the question of whether the partisan divide reflects different views of the trade-offs or cues from party leaders. In a new study with David Doherty, Conor Dowling, and Michael Miller, I address this with two survey experiments conducted in 2024. Respondents chose between two voting rules for a hypothetical town. Under one, every eligible resident voted, but so did some ineligible residents; under the other, no ineligible residents voted, but fewer eligible residents did. We randomly varied the numbers on each side, as well as which party was said to have proposed each rule.Respondents in these experiments treated an illegal vote as far weightier than a lost legal one, giving roughly as much weight to one ineligible ballot as to ten eligible citizens not voting, and Democrats and Republicans responded to these trade-offs in much the same way, although Republicans were 18 to 19 percentage points more likely to favor eliminating illegal votes. Party cues, however, had enormous effects: support for the rule that eliminated illegal voting rose by 37 to 48 percentage points when it was attributed to the respondent’s own party.These findings suggest that much of the partisan conflict over voting rules reflects signals from party leaders rather than fundamentally different values. Americans across the political spectrum place a high priority on keeping ineligible votes out of elections, which leaves more room for compromise than the current debate would suggest.Professor Milyo’s article, coauthored with David Doherty, Conor M. Dowling, and Michael G. Miller, is available Milyo’s work was funded in part by the Ulysses S. Grant Institute. | | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/9fecfe84a81b/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363969?e=dc5f639d62)

Hey friends,I’m thrilled to share a special Memphis double drop with all of you! Memphis is having a moment, and I wanted you to hear it straight from two people who are living it.
[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/12qFCWZj6af?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)****
****[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/uYsrjzJqtAu?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

First up is KeShaun Pearson, an organizer with Memphis Community Against Pollution and the brother of my good friend Rep. Justin J. Pearson. KeShaun lost both of his grandmothers to cancer in their early 60s, and he’ll tell you plainly why he believes environmental racism took them. That grief turned into knocking on doors in the rain with flyers printed at FedEx, and it’s still driving him today. We talk about Elon Musk’s xAI data centers, what happens to people’s trust when government sides with corporations over community, and who in the world responds to violent policy with civility.Then I sit down with Jerri Green, Memphis City Councilwoman and the Democratic nominee for governor. Jerri doesn’t take money from special interests, but she’ll tell you she has three: Bo, Vivian, and Wilder. We talk about what she hears from Tennesseans from Memphis to the mountains, her plans for day one, putting money back in your pocket instead of handing out corporate tax breaks, and a couple of stories about Marsha Blackburn that you’re going to have to hear to believe.Two different roles, one message: Memphis ain’t nothing to play with, and neither is Tennessee. Early voting runs through October 29th, and Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd. Make your plan to vote, bring somebody with you, and vote the whole ballot.

| | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when President Trump signs an executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: ** No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It targets how every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won.** _**They still are not stopping. **_ **The Constitution hasn't changed**. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is only one way to defend our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too. Chip in to help us keep fighting.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141929745/655238226/-569431239?refcode=261022-invented-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDUwOWQ2Ni0xOWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4c57c-RwlcZ8aQo0Pmj3PA3loNm-N8teN3t0AbWX2z8=)**

This evil administration is dead set on dismantling every critical program serving working people in need - programs that were a _lifeline_ for my family when I was growing up.
I know firsthand the crushing anxiety that comes with not knowing where your next meal will come from. It is unacceptable that any human being goes hungry in the richest country on earth.
**Sadly, my opponent Andy Barr and his idol Mitch McConnell voted for this.** They _proudly_ voted in favor of Trump's Big Beautiful Bill.
These cuts have already affected 24,655 children and 6,572 seniors in Kentucky - America's most vulnerable are being kicked aside while the wealthiest get tax cuts. It's not only illogical, but it's also despicable.
We can't afford to keep going on like this. I won't settle for one more child going hungry by way of this cruel administration.

Oct 22 | | | | | | | | | | | I want to echo something my friend, Governor Andy Beshear, called out recently. It's about your SNAP benefits. | | ---|---|--- This evil administration is dead set on dismantling every critical program serving working people in need - programs that were a lifeline for my family when I was growing up. I know firsthand the crushing anxiety that comes with not knowing where your next meal will come from. It is unacceptable that any human being goes hungry in the richest country on earth. Sadly, my opponent Andy Barr and his idol Mitch McConnell voted for this. They proudly voted in favor of Trump's Big Beautiful Bill. These cuts have already affected 24,655 children and 6,572 seniors in Kentucky - America's most vulnerable are being kicked aside while the wealthiest get tax cuts. It's not only illogical, but it's also despicable. We can't afford to keep going on like this. I won't settle for one more child going hungry by way of this cruel administration. Can you chip in whatever you can spare today to defeat Andy Barr, flip this seat BLUE, and halt Trump 's MAGA agenda in its tracks? No kid should ever go hungry. Charles | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Charles Booker P.O. Box 1, Louisville, KY 40201 ? ?

When a local prosecutor weighs immigration status in deciding charges and plea deals, two people who commit the same crime in the same community can face very different consequences. A House investigation and a Department of Justice civil rights probe now allege that's not a hypothetical -- it's policy, in writing, in jurisdictions from Northern Virginia to Colorado to Philadelphia.
Start in Fairfax County, Virginia. Commonwealth's Attorney Steve Descano's office adopted guidelines in December 2020 -- his first year in office -- instructing assistant prosecutors to consider immigration consequences where possible and where doing so accords with justice in plea bargaining, charging decisions, and sentencing. On May 6, 2026, the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division notified Descano it was opening an investigation to determine whether his office discriminated against United States citizens by offering preferential treatment only to illegal alien criminal defendants. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon put it bluntly: the Division "will not allow local prosecutors to pick and choose winners based on their immigration status," and the probe would examine "sweetheart deals to illegal immigrants charged with serious crimes."
Eight days later, Descano was on Capitol Hill testifying before the House Judiciary Committee's hearing, "Fairfax County, Virginia: The Dangerous Consequences of Sanctuary Policies." His answer to all of it: the policies are fair and legal, and the investigations are "political nonsense."...

body:
I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me one last time

|
---

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940247/655264389/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) Derek,

I know I’ve been sending you a lot of emails about my reelection race in Virginia these days, and today, I want to take a step back and reintroduce myself.

[_**But first, with just 12 days until Election Day, I'm hoping you'll consider chipping in to my reelection campaign to protect this must-win Senate seat for Democrats and take back control of Congress.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940248/655264391/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=)

Like so many Americans, I grew up in a middle-class family and was lucky enough to attend good public schools. I have my 8th grade history teacher to thank for setting me on the path to being a Democrat. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940250/655264392/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) Fast forward a few years, I became the first person in my family to graduate from college, made possible by working multiple jobs and taking out student loans.

Before I became a U.S. Senator, I actually started out in business. I invested my entire life savings, a few thousand dollars, into my first venture... which failed in about six weeks, by the way. My second venture did a little better, lasting six months, but it wasn’t until my third try that things started to look up. I’m extremely proud to have founded what became one of Virginia’s leading tech companies.

It was actually that experience that got me into public service. I thought that everybody in this country ought to have the same kind of fair shot that I had. So, I ran for governor in Virginia, and won. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940251/655264393/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) And if you can believe it, my good friend Tim Kaine (now my fellow Virginia senator) was my Lieutenant Governor. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940252/655264394/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) After our four years in the governor’s office, Virginia was rated the best state for business, the best managed state, _and_ the best state to receive an education. But even then, I knew that my work to make sure that _every_ family – no matter their background – has the same shot that I did, was far from over.

That’s when I ran for the United States Senate, and won. That year, President Obama won in Virginia too – the first time the Commonwealth of Virginia voted for a Democratic presidential nominee since 1964. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940253/655264396/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) In the Senate, I helped spearhead the largest infrastructure and public lands investments in half a century, worked to significantly expand Virginia’s domestic manufacturing, and have fought to lower health care costs across the Commonwealth. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940254/655264397/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) **But I have to tell you, in my time in the Senate – maybe in my time in politics – there has been nothing as challenging, as bizarre, and as _holy sugar_ as the second Trump administration.**

This administration's incompetence has made every American less safe. The president’s tariffs and reckless foreign policy have caused prices to skyrocket for working families. His administration is peddling conspiracy theories about our elections and undermining American’s faith in our democracy. And my Republican colleagues continue to fail at holding him accountable.

I didn’t get into politics to let people like Trump dismantle our federal government and rebuild it for himself and his allies. I’m proud to lead the fight against this corrupt administration, but I can’t do it alone.

[_**I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me one last time so I can keep up my work holding this administration accountable and delivering for Virginia. Can I count on you to pitch in to my campaign so we can win BIG on Election Day?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940256/655264398/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=)

The fight continues,

Mark Warner ********[Contribute](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940257/655264399/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=)********
