**GREENWICH, CT** -- Jonathan Goldstein, Republican candidate for Connecticut's 150th House District, is calling for answers after federal earnings data showed Connecticut's female-to-male median weekly earnings ratio falling from 97% in 2020 to 79.6% in 2025.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..1Mzdb4i7hzyJb-mv_Aobi40eH5pPpGBw6Mks5TUR9xw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221634630)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1ea202d9-ab86-4ec7-a476-8b06ba0bd64e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[View Campaign Site](https://substack.com/redirect/40dcd567-33c8-4784-82d1-e88bcbbca06d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Source USA Facts using Bureau of Labor Statistics Data](https://substack.com/redirect/ed80a465-e769-46c0-b1d1-d0035b2a0180?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"Six years ago, Connecticut women were earning approximately 97 cents for every dollar earned by men. Today, that figure is below 80 cents," Goldstein said. "What happened to equal opportunity, and why isn't Hartford demanding answers?"
According to Bureau of Labor Statistics data compiled by [USAFacts](https://substack.com/redirect/ed80a465-e769-46c0-b1d1-d0035b2a0180?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Connecticut's reported ratio declined by 17.4 percentage points. The figures do not establish the causes of the decline.
Goldstein contrasted Connecticut's performance with neighboring New York, where women working full-time, year-round earned 91.4 cents for every dollar earned by men in 2024, according to New York State Department of Labor data. Although the two figures use different statistical measures, Goldstein said the comparison raises important questions about economic opportunity.
**" This is bigger than national politics. New York doesn't appear to have the same problem to this extent. Connecticut has its own legislature, its own economy and its own responsibilities. Hartford needs to be held accountable."**
### **Economic Independence Is Also a Women 's Safety Issue**
Speaking during Domestic Violence Awareness Month, Goldstein connected the wage gap to women's financial independence and personal safety, an issue he raised at the League of Women Voters candidate forum.
"When women earn less, it becomes harder to afford housing, raise families, save for retirement or leave an abusive relationship. Economic independence is not just about opportunity. Sometimes it is about survival."
Greenwich's October 2026 Domestic Violence Awareness proclamation identifies domestic violence as the town's most-reported violent crime and reports more than 3,600 hotline calls to YWCA Greenwich Domestic Abuse Services during the preceding year.
"These are our mothers, daughters, sisters and neighbors. We need to ensure that women have both the economic opportunities and the public safety protections they deserve."
### **Affordability, Opportunity and Local Control**
Goldstein, _**who has received the endorsement of the Fraternal Order of Police**_ , said effective policing, victim protection and cooperation with local domestic violence organizations must remain priorities.
"Greenwich police officers and local service providers understand our community. Hartford should be supporting their ability to protect victims, not making their jobs harder."
Goldstein said the issue reflects his campaign's **ABCs: Affordability, Beaches and Local Control.**
"Affordability isn't just about what you pay. It's about what you earn, what you can save and whether you can afford to live independently."
Goldstein concluded:
**" Connecticut women deserve better than a widening wage gap and political excuses. Hartford needs to explain what happened, examine the causes and work toward real solutions.**
**" We need a Connecticut where women can earn a fair living, raise their families, build financial security and live safely. That's what equal opportunity should mean."**

#### **[Susan Collins Applauds Release of 315,000 Barrels from Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve](https://substack.com/redirect/36c102ee-30ab-49eb-bf2e-6de169a66e4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The Trump administration will release up to 315,000 barrels from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, a month after Sens. Susan Collins and Angus King asked for it. That's equal to a 13% supply increase for New England, and 200,000 of the reserve's barrels sit in South Portland. As some forecasters are privately warning that home heating oil could reach $8.00 per gallon this winter, the hope is that surplus supply will bid down the cost. In 26 years, the reserve has been tapped only twice, in 2011 to swap in cleaner oil and in 2012 after Hurricane Sandy. This is the first time it's been used to bring prices down. [Seamus Othot has the story](https://substack.com/redirect/36c102ee-30ab-49eb-bf2e-6de169a66e4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

#### **[Waterville Police Arrest Suspect After He Threatened to Murder Officers During Six-Hour Standoff](https://substack.com/redirect/6c827b9c-0bc5-46cb-9893-8a0a4e201f9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Waterville police went to 10 Autumn St. around 6 p.m. Tuesday with a terrorizing warrant for John Whitney, 41, over threats he allegedly made online. Police say he wouldn't open the door, threatened to shoot officers, and after several hours of negotiating started throwing knives at them. The State Police tactical team came in around 11 p.m., and an hour later Whitney was in custody. Police say he faces five charges, including aggravated reckless conduct and criminal threatening with a dangerous weapon. Corrections records show a John Whitney of the same age on probation in Waterville, sentenced in 2025 to three years for assaulting a police officer and let out early on probation. Those conditions barred him from having dangerous weapons. It isn't confirmed he's the same man.

#### **[Oft-Arrested Litchfield Man Busted Again After Fleeing Police With Incorrect Plates](https://substack.com/redirect/ee68fe4e-b36b-4371-8efb-dae1144f809b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
A Kennebec deputy in Augusta ran the plates on a Subaru Outback Monday night and they came back to a BMW X5. Deputies say the driver went the wrong way down a one-way street, then led them toward Belgrade at more than 80 mph before bailing out on foot on West Road. The deputy recognized him: Joshua Tilley, 43, of Litchfield, whom he had arrested several times before. Deputies say Tilley faces seven charges, including violating conditions of release, driving to endanger and attaching false plates, and is held without bail. He was arrested in 2019 after he allegedly kidnapped his girlfriend and fled police.
#### **[Lisbon Drunk Driver Crashes Into Building Then Utility Pole Before Being Arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/610256b8-60f2-48de-8b4c-6cb749a52a4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Lisbon police say a car left Route 196 around 6:22 p.m. Sunday, hit a building near School Street, kept going and took out a utility pole near Aubuchon Hardware, dropping power lines. Lisbon Street stayed closed until 11:22 p.m. Police say Joseph St. Amant, 70, of Lisbon, was charged with OUI. The next night, another car on Route 196 hit a two-unit apartment building on School Street. That driver went to the hospital, police haven't named him or her, and charges are expected.

#### **[Portland School Official's Dog Proposal: Puppies Behind Plexiglass?](https://substack.com/redirect/86d2d5ee-62d1-49ae-b82d-d7d155d8563f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
A follow-up to Tuesday's item. At the Oct. 14 Portland Public Schools policy committee meeting, assistant superintendent Abdullahi Ahmed asked that students opt in to dog activities, such as therapy-animal events, rather than parents having to opt them out, citing Islamic teaching that "dog saliva is considered impure." The meeting ran an hour. The board's most creative idea came from member Maya Lena, who floated keeping the puppies in a plexiglass enclosure so students "could interact with the puppies without touching the dogs or getting their fluids on them."

## Maine Wire TV
**If you 're reading this, you probably get Maine Wire TV delivered via Substack. But you can also watch us on Facebook, X, and YouTube. You can subscribe on Apple or Spotify, too! Here's yesterday's episode...**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/dd611a99-0f6b-4f87-8413-c557ba0588d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**[Jon Fetherston's Lewiston City Hall Confrontation](https://substack.com/redirect/d6e84895-d2fc-4cd3-ada1-1a540d62c190?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**: Tom Shattuck hosts Jon Fetherston, Seamus Othot, Graham and me. Jon describes a voter at Lewiston City Hall who told him to meet him in the street, his exchange with Safiya Khalid, and the translators helping voters, many of whom he says registered the same day. I walk through how Chinese-run illegal marijuana grows use the hemp loophole to sell out of state.
## Today's Political Events

Oct 22 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- The Trump administration will release up to 315,000 barrels from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, a month after Sens. Susan Collins and Angus King asked for it. That's equal to a 13% supply increase for New England, and 200,000 of the reserve's barrels sit in South Portland. As some forecasters are privately warning that home heating oil could reach $8.00 per gallon this winter, the hope is that surplus supply will bid down the cost. In 26 years, the reserve has been tapped only twice, in 2011 to swap in cleaner oil and in 2012 after Hurricane Sandy. This is the first time it's been used to bring prices down. . Like this kind of reporting? Subscribe to The Robinson Report for the latest news moving Maine politics. Subscribe free at RobinsonReport.Substack.com Waterville police went to 10 Autumn St. around 6 p.m. Tuesday with a terrorizing warrant for John Whitney, 41, over threats he allegedly made online. Police say he wouldn't open the door, threatened to shoot officers, and after several hours of negotiating started throwing knives at them. The State Police tactical team came in around 11 p.m., and an hour later Whitney was in custody. Police say he faces five charges, including aggravated reckless conduct and criminal threatening with a dangerous weapon. Corrections records show a John Whitney of the same age on probation in Waterville, sentenced in 2025 to three years for assaulting a police officer and let out early on probation. Those conditions barred him from having dangerous weapons. It isn't confirmed he's the same man. | | ---|---|--- A Kennebec deputy in Augusta ran the plates on a Subaru Outback Monday night and they came back to a BMW X5. Deputies say the driver went the wrong way down a one-way street, then led them toward Belgrade at more than 80 mph before bailing out on foot on West Road. The deputy recognized him: Joshua Tilley, 43, of Litchfield, whom he had arrested several times before. Deputies say Tilley faces seven charges, including violating conditions of release, driving to endanger and attaching false plates, and is held without bail. He was arrested in 2019 after he allegedly kidnapped his girlfriend and fled police. Lisbon police say a car left Route 196 around 6:22 p.m. Sunday, hit a building near School Street, kept going and took out a utility pole near Aubuchon Hardware, dropping power lines. Lisbon Street stayed closed until 11:22 p.m. Police say Joseph St. Amant, 70, of Lisbon, was charged with OUI. The next night, another car on Route 196 hit a two-unit apartment building on School Street. That driver went to the hospital, police haven't named him or her, and charges are expected. | | ---|---|--- A follow-up to Tuesday's item. At the Oct. 14 Portland Public Schools policy committee meeting, assistant superintendent Abdullahi Ahmed asked that students opt in to dog activities, such as therapy-animal events, rather than parents having to opt them out, citing Islamic teaching that "dog saliva is considered impure." The meeting ran an hour. The board's most creative idea came from member Maya Lena, who floated keeping the puppies in a plexiglass enclosure so students "could interact with the puppies without touching the dogs or getting their fluids on them." Are we seeking freedom--or grieving the foundations that make it meaningful?
The kitchen table is our first crucible. There, we learn the weight of our voices and the gravity of responsibility. We discover that love is not a transaction, and our choices ripple toward those bound to us.
Erich Fromm explored how freedom can bring isolation, tempting us to trade our judgment for the certainty of belonging. We often mistake the constraints of connection for the chains of oppression. Yet, in escaping obligation, we risk weakening the very foundations that help us stand.
Family is where love, duty, and conflict meet. Traditions can burden us, but viewing family solely as an obstacle to independence is a dangerous trade. A healthy family gives us roots and the courage to meet the world without losing ourselves.
Freedom is the capacity to choose, to care, and to remain accountable.
**Pause. Breathe. Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

# This is it, Friend
---
| | | | | | Friend,
This is it. In just a few days, this campaign comes down to the wire, and October 27 is our final fundraising deadline before New Mexicans finish casting their ballots.I'll be straight with you about what that deadline means. Every dollar we raise before October 27 decides how long we stay on the air in the final stretch. Television, digital, mail: those are the voters we reach, or the voters we don't.
My opponent has deep pockets and national money behind her. We have something better: thousands of New Mexicans who believe this state can be safer, more affordable, and run by someone who has actually delivered results. I spent twelve years as Mayor of Rio Rancho proving that. I showed up to answer the tough questions at the KOB debate when my opponent didn't. And I am going to keep showing up all the way to Election Day.
But I can't do it without you.
Whatever you can spare today, whether that's $25, $50, $100, or more, goes straight to keeping our message in front of voters through the final days of this race. If you've already given, thank you. If you can give one more time before the deadline, now is when it matters most.

name: Josh Shapiro
subject: Got a question?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA]
body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek,

Since we kicked off this reelection campaign
nearly ten months ago, I’ve heard from so many Pennsylvanians from all
across our Commonwealth. I’ve heard your stories, your concerns, and your
kind words.

But I’ve also heard a lot of questions — so I wanted to use this email to
address some FAQs about this final stretch of the election. (But listen,
if you’re already up-to-date on everything going on here in Pennsylvania,
[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19746?t=1001&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]please use this link to rush a donation before midnight. Every dollar
counts!)

Question 1: What is the state of the race right now?

It’s... complex, to say the least. If you only paid attention to the polls
and the pundits, they’d tell you we’re in the lead right now. And sure,
Derek, I think
we’re in the lead too. But here in Pennsylvania — the most competitive
battleground state in the country — leads have a tendency to evaporate. At
the very last second.

So throughout these final twelve days, we’re going to run this race
full-speed ahead: TV ads, on-the-ground organizers, rallies, events. All
of it makes a difference, and all of it takes resources.

Question 2: What makes this election different?

Look, I believe any election in Pennsylvania is important. But this
Governor’s race in 2026? It’s not only about Pennsylvania’s future. It’s
about our entire country’s future. Our entire democracy’s future.

If my opponent wins on November 3rd, Republicans will control every
state-level office in Pennsylvania. So come 2028, when Donald Trump almost
certainly tries to cast doubt on our elections and lean on his enablers to
undermine them? We need a Governor who will stand up to him — not someone
who will help him overturn an election.

Question 3: How can I help?

The best way to make an impact at this point in the election is to [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19746?t=1002&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]make
a donation of any amount to our campaign — seriously, even just one dollar
makes a difference! Trust me, I wish it didn’t take so much money to win
an election either. But my opponent has the full backing of Donald Trump
and his network of Mar-a-Lago donors. And the only way we can fight back
against that kind of cash is with an overwhelming, effective response.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19746?t=1003&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]So Derek, if
any of those answers convinced you, will you chip in as much as you can to
make these final twelve days count? In a state like Pennsylvania, your
donation could literally be the difference between winning and losing.

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19747?t=1004&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $5 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19748?t=1005&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $15 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19749?t=1006&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $25 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19750?t=1007&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $50 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19751?t=1008&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $100 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19746?t=1009&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Other →

Thank you,

Josh Shapiro
